small_guidance:
- The kernel currently launches one program per (N, C, Dp, Hp) = 32·64·8·16 = 262144 programs, each doing only ~64 elements of work — launch overhead dominates. Tile multiple Hp (and possibly Dp) rows per program, e.g. process a full (Dp, Hp) plane per (N, C) program with a 2D block, so each program amortizes more work.
- Add `@triton.autotune` over `num_warps ∈ {2, 4, 8}` and a few BLOCK_HP tile sizes; with W=64 the per-row reduction is tiny, so `num_warps=2` may win. Keep `num_stages=2`.
- The conv_transpose3d output is large (32·64·32·64·64 ≈ 256MB) and likely dominates runtime — verify with a profile; if so, tuning the epilogue further has limited headroom.
large_guidance:
- The torch ConvTranspose3d almost certainly dominates the 20ms runtime (the fused epilogue touches ~256MB once). Replace it with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile), computing the input×weight outer product and scattering into the strided output grid with stride=2, padding=1, output_padding=1. Fuse sum_weight + LayerNorm + AvgPool + GELU directly into the output write so the large intermediate is never materialized.
- Alternatively, since the LayerNorm normalizes only over the C=64 channel-axis-equivalent (here W=64 since norm_shape=(out_channels,) is applied on the last dim after a layout that puts channels last — verify), consider a gather-style direct conv-transpose that writes channels-last so the LN reduction is contiguous and can be fused entirely in registers.
- Pick the fusion boundary at the pooled output: each program computes one (N, C, Dp, Hp, Wp) element by accumulating the 2×2×2 pre-pool window values, each of which requires computing one conv-transpose output element from input × weight contributions. This eliminates the giant intermediate entirely and is the high-headroom redesign.
